# The t-test

::: {.callout-note}
## Video
Coming soon.
:::

**In this chapter:** compare the means of two groups and read the output.

```{r}
morph <- read.csv("data/morphometry.csv")
morph$Height <- morph$Height / 10
```

## Question and plot

Do males and females differ in height? Plot first:

```{r}
boxplot(Height ~ Sex, data = morph, ylab = "Height (cm)")
```

## Run the test

```{r}
t.test(Height ~ Sex, data = morph)
```

## Read the output

Start with the size of the difference, not the p-value.

- **Sample estimates:** the mean height is 159.9 cm for females and 175.0 cm for males, so males are about 15.1 cm taller.
- **95 percent confidence interval:** -16.7 to -13.4. The difference is female minus male, hence negative. A plausible range for the true difference is 13.4 to 16.7 cm.
- **p-value:** below 0.001. A difference this large would be very unlikely if the true means were equal.

Write it up with the estimate first:

> Males were on average 15.1 cm taller than females (95% CI 13.4 to 16.7 cm; Welch t-test, t = 18.2, d.f. = 152.8, p < 0.001).

## Your turn

Using `cholesterol.csv`, test whether cholesterol differs between the control and drug groups. Plot it first. How big is the difference, what is its confidence interval, and what would you conclude?
